articles.summary: Enhanced cloud-native network functions and new eBPF observability help operators move critical services to Kubernetes while improving security, performance, and visibility F5 (NASDAQ: FFIV), the global leader in delivering and securing every app and API, today announced enhanced cloud-native network functions and new observability capabilities that help service providers modernize critical network services as they move from virtualized infrastructure to Kubernetes and cloud-native architectures . Service providers are under pressure to support growing 5G, edge, IT, and emerging AI workloads, boost efficiency, and maintain the performance, security, and operational control required for carrier-grade services. Moving network functions to Kubernetes lets operators use infrastructure more flexibly but also introduces additional requirements for traffic management, security, lifecycle operations, and visibility across increasingly distributed environments. Autonomous AI models can scan, discover, and exploit vulnerabilities at machine speed. With the vulnerability exploit window now inverting to negative 7 days, attacks routinely begin before a software vendor even releases a patch.
